problem.statement: Legacy WinForms/.NET code that uses WeakReference to avoid event-subscription memory leaks can still resolve and invoke methods on a disposed IDisposable target during the gap before GC runs, causing unexpected behavior with no built-in way to check disposal state.

context.situation: A maintainer of a legacy WinForms app has a controller that tracks UI controls via WeakReference (to avoid an earlier memory leak from event subscriptions), but disposed controls can still be resolved and called against before garbage collection removes them.

current_workarounds: Switched controls from subscribing to controller events to being tracked via WeakReference, to avoid the original memory leak (this workaround introduced the new disposed-object race)

possible_wedges.offer: Roslyn/IDE analyzer that flags WeakReference<T> usages where T : IDisposable and warns about the disposed-but-not-yet-collected race, as part of a legacy-code audit rule set.
Audit CLI (OwnAudit) that scans a .NET/WPF/WinForms solution for WeakReference<IDisposable> patterns and reports the disposed-before-GC risk in an audit findings report.

risks: Single evidence item (n=1); unclear if this recurs across other legacy .NET codebases
Commercial intent signal is near zero (0.05) and commitment is 0 -- reads as a one-off technical question, not a purchase signal
No named substitute tools mentioned, so unclear whether existing static analyzers already cover this
Pain/urgency are moderate-low, suggesting an occasional annoyance rather than a recurring blocker worth paying to fix
